title: Eventual equality of maps from a finite-type module over a quasi-compact open
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its open subsets. Work in the category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set, let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{ji}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_j)_{i\le j}$ be a diagram, and let $(\mathcal F,(c_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F)_i)$ be a colimit cocone in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open (every open cover of $U$ has a finite subcover), and let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O|_U$-module of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]: every point of $U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ with an epimorphism $(\mathcal O|_V)^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_V$ for some finite $n\ge0$. Restriction of a module sheaf to $U$ means its values and restriction maps on the opens contained in $U$. For $i,j\in I$ and $\mathcal O|_U$-linear maps $g:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F_i|_U$ and $g\prime:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F_j|_U$ satisfying $(c_i|_U)\circ g=(c_j|_U)\circ g\prime$, there is $k\ge i,j$ such that $(\varphi_{ki}|_U)\circ g=(\varphi_{kj}|_U)\circ g\prime$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $\mathcal G$, no quasi-separatedness of $U$, and no injectivity of the transitions are assumed.

source.place: Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of (2): local eventual equality, a finite subcover, and a common upper bound; applied to the images of finitely many local generators of a module. This finite-type strengthening of the equality part of Modules Tag 01BS (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit) is the worker formulation.

proof.text: Forget the module structures. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-directed-colimit-underlying-sets], the underlying sheaf of sets of $\mathcal F$ with its specified legs is still a colimit. Put $P(W)=\varinjlim_{a\in I}\mathcal F_a(W)$ as a presheaf of sets. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-colimit-sheafification], $P^\#$ with the composites of the presheaf coprojections and the sheafification unit is another such colimit. The unique colimit isomorphism $P^\#\simeq\mathcal F$ identifies these composites with $c_a$: the maps in the two directions induced by the cocones compose to identities by uniqueness in the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

For two stage sections with equal colimit images, use the colimit isomorphism of step 1 to identify their images under the sheafification unit. The local-equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] is supplied directly in Lean by Mathlib's Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective instance for toSheafify and Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem. At a given point, choose a member of the resulting covering equalizer sieve. Naturality of the presheaf colimit coprojections and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] give an index above both stages on which the restricted sections agree. No compactness is needed in this step.

source.place: Tag 009F (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of (2), local-equality argument before extracting a finite subcover; Sites Tags 00WB and 00WK; Categories Tag 04AX

proof.text: Fix $x\in U$. The finite-type hypothesis and [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], clause (1), give an open $V_x\subseteq U$ containing $x$, sections $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in\mathcal G(V_x)$, and an epimorphism $e_x:(\mathcal O|_{V_x})^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_{V_x}$ with $e_x(e_r)=t_r$. For each $r$, the sections $g(t_r)$ and $g\prime(t_r)$ have equal images in $\mathcal F(V_x)$ by the assumed equality of morphisms. Apply step 2 at $x$ for each of these finitely many pairs. Intersect the resulting neighbourhoods and choose a common upper bound $a_x\ge i,j$ for their indices. We obtain an open $x\in T_x\subseteq V_x$ on which the two maps to $\mathcal F_{a_x}$ agree on every $t_r$. When $n=0$, take $T_x=V_x$ and any upper bound of $i,j$.

source.place: Tag 01B5 (definition-finite-type); finite-generator application of the local-equality part of Sheaves Tag 009F

proof.text: Use categorical epimorphism cancellation instead of assuming sectionwise surjectivity. If Q is a generating neighbourhood from [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] and T is the smaller neighbourhood from step 3, restrict further over the object (T → Q) of the site Over Q using Mathlib's overFunctor. It is a left adjoint and preserves colimits and epimorphisms. Cancel the restricted generating epimorphism from the free module. The restricted free coproduct cocone is still colimiting by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so equality after it is checked on each restricted rank-one summand. Maps from the rank-one module are determined by the image of 1, namely the corresponding generating section. Its value on every object below T is the restriction of its value on T by compatibility of global sections. Naturality and linearity now give equality on every summand, hence equality of the restricted morphisms and all their components on opens below T. The empty generating family is handled by the same coproduct universal property.

source.place: Section Tag 01AF (section-kernels) and Lemma Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian): epimorphisms of O_X-modules are the surjective maps of sheaves, i.e. locally surjective; finite free modules as in Modules Tag 01B5

proof.text: The opens $T_x$ cover $U$. Quasi-compactness supplies a finite subcover $T_{x_1},\ldots,T_{x_m}$. Directedness gives $k\ge i,j,a_{x_1},\ldots,a_{x_m}$. Composing the equalities of step 4 with $\varphi_{k a_{x_b}}$ and using the diagram identities gives equality of $(\varphi_{ki}|_U)\circ g$ and $(\varphi_{kj}|_U)\circ g\prime$ on every member of the finite cover. For an arbitrary open $W\subseteq U$ and section of $\mathcal G(W)$ their images therefore agree on the cover $(W\cap T_{x_b})_b$ of $W$, and hence agree by the sheaf axiom for $\mathcal F_k$. This is the required equality of morphisms. If $U=\varnothing$, choose any $k\ge i,j$ and use uniqueness of sections on the empty open. No intersection of covering opens has been assumed quasi-compact.
